# Skills and README for multi-repo suites

## What to build

`graph-execution suite` is gaining support for features in **different git repos** (for example a backend and a frontend). The rules users and agents need to know:

- Each feature belongs to exactly one repo: the git root of its tasks folder. `--feature` takes `<tasks-dir>:<prd>` as today; absolute paths into other repos work.
- The command can run from **any folder**, a repo or not. The suite folder is `<launch-folder>/.graph-execution/suite-<id>/` (the launch folder's git root when it is inside a repo). `list`, `open`, `clean` and `suite --resume` are run from that same folder.
- Each repo gets its own `suite/<id>` branch with only its own features merged. Then **one e2e phase** runs on a combined folder holding every repo's result side by side (`<suite folder>/e2e/workspace/<repo-name>/`); the e2e tester starts every app itself, on ports the suite assigns per repo (listed at the top of the e2e spec), and the fixer can fix any repo.
- Each repo uses its own `graph-execution.config.json` for `setup`, `validate`, `validateParallel`, `validateAt`, `keepRuns`. Suite-wide settings (`concurrency`, `e2eReview`, `humanReview`, `loopDetection`, `attempts`, `validationRounds`, `fixPasses`) come from the launch folder's config, or flags and defaults.
- **All or nothing:** the result is applied to every repo (as uncommitted changes on the branch each was on) or to none, when any repo can't take it (detached HEAD, on another branch, or a conflict); the log names the repo.
- Features in different repos never see each other's code while they run. A frontend feature that calls a new backend API must have the **contract** (endpoints, payloads, env vars) written into both PRDs.
- `clean` inside one of the repos never deletes a live suite's branches (each non-home repo has a pointer file `.graph-execution/_suites/<suite-id>.json`). `clean <suite-id>` from the launch folder removes everything in every repo and skips a repo that is gone, with a warning. `--resume` stops when a recorded repo is gone.

Update the two bundled skills and the README so they describe this. This task changes only Markdown files.

## Context: files to read before implementing

- `skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md` (lines 12–20) — "One PRD or several": the suite rules for several PRDs; add the multi-repo case here
- `skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md` (lines 82–90 and the final "tell the user" step near the end) — where task folders are written and the suite command shown
- `skills/run-graph/SKILL.md` (lines 10–48) — run or suite, arguments, launch commands
- `skills/run-graph/SKILL.md` (lines 50–70) — what to tell the user about a suite
- `README.md` (lines 379–425) — the "Suites" section: bullet list, the `--web` page, `--resume`, and "What a suite produces"
- `README.md` (lines 455–480) — the skills section mentioning several PRDs and `run-graph`
- `docs/prd/13-multi-repo-suites.md` — the full design, for anything unclear
- `src/install/skills.ts` (line 25) — `skills/` is copied into users' projects as is: keep the skills self-contained (no links into `src/`)

## Patterns to follow

**Skill voice:** short imperative sentences, bold lead words in bullets, concrete commands in fenced `bash` blocks, as in `skills/run-graph/SKILL.md`.

**README voice:** bullets with a bold lead (`- **One child run per feature.** ...`), then a code block of what is produced, as in `README.md:385–421`.

## Step-by-step tasks

### UPDATE `skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md`

- **IMPLEMENT**: under "One PRD or several", a bullet **Features in several repos**: when PRDs target different repos, write each feature's task folder inside its own repo (`<repo>/.agents/tasks/<feature>/`), never one folder per repo for a cross-repo feature; split a PRD that spans repos into one feature per repo; write the shared contract (endpoints, request/response shapes, env vars, ports are assigned by the suite) verbatim into both PRDs; tell the user which repos the suite spans. In the final step, show the multi-repo command with absolute paths:
  ```bash
  npx graph-execution suite --feature /abs/shop-api/.agents/tasks/export-api:/abs/shop-api/PRD-export-api.md --feature /abs/shop-web/.agents/tasks/export-ui:/abs/shop-web/PRD-export-ui.md --provider claude
  ```
- **VALIDATE**: read the file top to bottom; the existing single-repo instructions must be unchanged

### UPDATE `skills/run-graph/SKILL.md`

- **IMPLEMENT**: in "Work out the arguments", say features may be in different repos and that `--feature` paths are then absolute; the suite runs from the current folder, which need not be a repo, and later `open`, `list`, `clean`, `--resume` must run from that same folder. In "Warn, don't block, about uncommitted code" note that every repo is checked. In what to tell the user about a suite, add one bullet for multi-repo: per-repo integration, one combined e2e phase, all-or-nothing apply.
- **VALIDATE**: read the file; commands stay one per fenced block

### UPDATE `README.md`

- **IMPLEMENT**: in "Suites", a sub-section **Features in several repos** with the rules listed in "What to build", an example command with absolute paths run from a parent folder, and the produced layout:
  ```
  <launch-folder>/.graph-execution/suite-<id>/   # suite.json (with repos[]), lock, run.log, features/, logs/
    e2e/workspace/<repo-name>/                   # each repo's suite/<id> worktree, side by side
  <each repo>/suite/<id>                         # branch: that repo's features, then the e2e fixes
  <each other repo>/.graph-execution/_suites/<suite-id>.json   # pointer, keeps clean from deleting live branches
  ```
  Update the skills paragraph (around line 464) with one sentence on several repos.
- **IMPLEMENT**: if the build renders the README (`scripts/render-readme.mjs`), check it still renders: `npm run build`.
- **VALIDATE**: `npm run build && npx vitest run src/readme src/install`

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `skills/to-tasks/SKILL.md` explains where a multi-repo suite's task folders go, splitting cross-repo PRDs, and writing the contract into both PRDs, and shows the absolute-path command
- [ ] `skills/run-graph/SKILL.md` covers absolute `--feature` paths, launching from any folder, and the multi-repo outcome
- [ ] `README.md` "Suites" documents features in several repos, config split, all-or-nothing apply, the layout, and lifecycle commands from the launch folder
- [ ] No existing single-repo instruction is removed or changed in meaning
- [ ] `npm run build`, `npx vitest run src/readme src/install` pass

## Validation commands

```bash
npm run build
npx vitest run src/readme src/install
```
